src/render/menu.ts lines 117-118: loadTerrainProps(...).then((p) => terrain.setProps(p ?? {})) and the loadTerrainLandmarks .then() run even when that menu terrain was already disposed (menu.build again or a match started). Guard both callbacks with `if (this.terrain !== terrain) { for (const g of Object.values(p ?? {}).flat()) g.dispose(); return; }` (and skip adding the landmarks in that case). For information, a dependency in src/render/terrain.ts. FRAY's hour_stone.glb is exported sunk 1.2 m (landmarks_art2.py SINK), because loadTerrainLandmarks stands a landmark on groundAt(), which inside its own non-replaced wall block is the block's top (wallHeights.hourStones 1.2). The stone encloses that cliff block. If terrain.ts ever lets a landmark replace a rotated wall (an OBB test) or stops lifting landmarks onto wall tops, the hour-stone must be re-exported without SINK. Separately, there are 12 new flush camp-lip landmarks on RIFT (each 1 draw, 340-460 tris, a 512 atlas) for your perf sweep.

Make culling of wide, flat landmarks tighter in src/render/terrain.ts. At the low-road fight (101.52,95.6) the south skirt modules still draw 8,902 main-pass tris and about 4.8k shadow tris, but none of their pixels are on screen (_harness/_shots/fw_W5a_ref1_rift_edge_at5.png shows no skirt). The cause is bounding spheres.

(1) Shadow casters. caster() stores `top: sp.center.y + sp.radius`. For a 22 x 14 m module that is 3.8 m tall, that gives top about 13 m. cullCasters then uses k = top*0.5, which inflates both the sun shift and the radius (+ sl*k). Take `top` from the world bounding box instead: geometry.boundingBox applied to matrixWorld, then .max.y.

(2) Main pass. Optionally, for loadTerrainLandmarks meshes, set frustumCulled=false and toggle visible each frame with a world-Box3 test against the view frustum, the same way the casters are handled. three's sphere test, with a radius of about 13 m, admits modules whose boxes are outside the view.

The verifier proposed a 'shadow: false' content flag for off-map skirts. I did not add it to content/maps, because it would remove the Dialwood crowns' contact shadows on the skirt beds. If you still want the flag after (1), implement it in loadTerrainLandmarks and W5a will set it on the entries.
